Booking terms

Booking, Payment & Cancellation Policy

Use this page to understand the payment sequence, route-change boundaries, and Travel Credit logic before money moves. It is designed to reduce ambiguity around planning, not create it.

Deposit

Dates are only secured once the booking is funded

A deposit is the point where crew scheduling, vehicle planning, and route handling become operational commitments instead of provisional planning.

Balance

Final payment should clarify, not surprise

The remaining balance follows the booking documents and should happen after the route scope, handling, and readiness steps are clear.

Changes

Travel Credit is the main flexibility mechanism

When plans move, the goal is to protect operational certainty while still preserving value for the guest wherever the policy allows it.

Booking sequence

Treat the route page and voucher as the decision baseline

Booking should not begin from a price alone. Route fit, readiness requirements, and operating conditions should be visible before a payment request becomes a commitment.

  • Use the tour page to confirm the route shape, origin, and pace.
  • Use the travel guide when the route includes Ijen, weather-sensitive access, or physical constraints.
  • Treat the issued booking documents as the final operational reference for the confirmed booking.

Payment handling

Deposits secure planning. They do not replace route clarity.

The deposit exists to reserve dates and logistics. The final balance should follow the timing and methods described in your booking documents, not informal assumptions.

  • JVTO operates private handling by default, so the booking secures crew and vehicle allocation for your group.
  • The balance timing depends on the confirmed route and booking documentation.
  • The written quote and voucher should state what is covered before the balance is due.

Reschedules & cancellations

Flexibility follows written rules, not ad hoc negotiation

Changes close to departure affect permits, rooming, and crew scheduling. That is why the policy uses structured windows and Travel Credit instead of improvised exceptions.

  • Travel Credit is the main mechanism when the booking remains eligible for value preservation.
  • Very late changes or no-shows can fall outside that protection because the route is already being executed.
  • Health, weather, or access restrictions should be read alongside the relevant support pages, not in isolation.

If the route includes Ijen or weather-sensitive access, read the health screening and closures pages alongside this policy before treating the booking as fully settled.
